name: Sufism
summary: Sufism is the mystical tradition of Islam, in which Muslims seek direct personal experience of God through a path of repentance, asceticism, remembrance of God and guidance by a master. It grew as a counterweight to worldliness, prizes poverty and self-discipline, and holds to the divine law while opposing the dry legalism of the lawyer-divines. Its sources say little about the organisation of the state.
scope: The tradition of Islamic mysticism (tasawwuf) as defined by Britannica (Schimmel) and the New Catholic Encyclopedia entry on Sufism, with al-Hujwiri's Kashf al-Mahjub, the oldest Persian treatise on Sufism, as its own text. Individual Sufi orders that took part in politics (Sanusiyya, Bektashiyya) are other subjects and are not used. Thinkers outside the saved sources (Ibn al-Arabi, al-Ghazali's Revival, Rumi's Masnavi) were not read for answers.
